newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Hibernia partners start drilling. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Canada's Hibernia partners start drilling. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]

text.p: Partners in Canada's Hibernia offshore oil project said on Monday they began drilling the operation's first development well (corrects to add dropped word "first"), 19 days ahead of schedule.
The C$5.8 billion project's backers said the well spudded on Monday was the first drilled at the site, about 315 km southeast of St. John's, since exploration drilling in the 1980s.

"Drilling 19 days ahead of schedule is quite an achievement when you consider that the platform was installed only seven weeks ago, on June 6, and our drillers and other offshore personnel were on board about a week later," said Harvey Smith, president of the project's operating company, Hibernia Management and Development Co.
First oil from the project was sheduled for December and peak output was expected to be 135,000 barrels of oil a day from reserves of 615 million barrels.
It is the first of several major offshore oil and gas projects planned off Canada's east coast.

Partners in Hibernia are Petro-Canada's Petro-Canada Hibernia Partnership with 20 percent, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada Ltd with 33.125 percent, Chevron Corp unit Chevron Canada Resources Ltd with 26.875 percent, Murphy Oil Corp 's Murphy Atlantic Offshore Oil Co Ltd with 6.5 percent, the government of Canada's Canada Hibernia Holding Corp with 8.5 percent and Norsk Hydro A/S with five percent.
